BSGS of tensor symmetries

Source: R/tensor-can.R
tensor-bsgs.Rd

Ports of SymPy's BSGS constructors for tensor slot symmetries. get_symmetric_group_sgs(n, antisym) is the minimal BSGS of a (anti)symmetric tensor of rank n; bsgs_direct_product() is the direct product of two BSGS; get_transversals() gives the basic transversals of a BSGS; get_minimal_bsgs() recomputes a BSGS with minimal base (or NULL); tensor_gens() is the BSGS of n tensors of the same type, with fixed slots list_free_indices and commutation symmetry sym; gens_products() combines tensors of different types, each given as list(base_i, gens_i, free_i, sym_i). riemann_bsgs is the BSGS of the Riemann tensor.

Usage

bsgs_direct_product(base1, gens1, base2, gens2, signed = TRUE)

get_symmetric_group_sgs(n, antisym = FALSE)

riemann_bsgs

get_transversals(base, gens)

get_minimal_bsgs(base, gens)

tensor_gens(base, gens, list_free_indices, sym = 0)

gens_products(...)

Format

riemann_bsgs: list(base, gens) for the Riemann tensor.

Arguments

signed

Whether the permutations are signed.

n

Rank of the tensor.

antisym

FALSE for a symmetric, TRUE for an antisymmetric tensor.

base, base1, base2

Bases (0 based integer vectors).

gens, gens1, gens2

Strong generators (lists of permutations).

list_free_indices

List of the slots occupied by fixed indices, one integer vector per tensor.

sym

Commutation symmetry: NULL, 0 or 1.

...

Tensor types, each list(base_i, gens_i, free_i, sym_i).

Value

get_symmetric_group_sgs(), bsgs_direct_product() and get_minimal_bsgs() return list(base, gens); tensor_gens() and gens_products() return list(size, base, gens); get_transversals() returns a list of named lists (point to array form).

Examples

get_symmetric_group_sgs(3)
#> [[1]]
#> [1] 0 1
#> 
#> [[2]]
#> [[2]][[1]]
#> (4)(0 1)
#> 
#> [[2]][[2]]
#> (4)(1 2)
#> 
#> 
b1 <- get_symmetric_group_sgs(1); b2 <- get_symmetric_group_sgs(2)
bsgs_direct_product(b1[[1]], b1[[2]], b2[[1]], b2[[2]])
#> [[1]]
#> [1] 1
#> 
#> [[2]]
#> [[2]][[1]]
#> (4)(1 2)
#> 
#> 
get_transversals(riemann_bsgs[[1]], riemann_bsgs[[2]])
#> [[1]]
#> [[1]]$`0`
#> [1] 0 1 2 3 4 5
#> 
#> [[1]]$`1`
#> [1] 1 0 2 3 5 4
#> 
#> [[1]]$`2`
#> [1] 2 3 0 1 4 5
#> 
#> [[1]]$`3`
#> [1] 3 2 0 1 5 4
#> 
#> 
#> [[2]]
#> [[2]]$`2`
#> [1] 0 1 2 3 4 5
#> 
#> [[2]]$`3`
#> [1] 0 1 3 2 5 4
#> 
#> 
b3 <- get_symmetric_group_sgs(3)
tensor_gens(b3[[1]], b3[[2]], list(1, 0))
#> [[1]]
#> [1] 8
#> 
#> [[2]]
#> [1] 0 4
#> 
#> [[3]]
#> [[3]][[1]]
#> (7)(0 2)
#> 
#> [[3]][[2]]
#> (7)(4 5)
#> 
#> 
gens_products(list(b2[[1]], b2[[2]], list(integer(), integer()), 0))
#> [[1]]
#> [1] 6
#> 
#> [[2]]
#> [1] 0 2
#> 
#> [[3]]
#> [[3]][[1]]
#> (5)(0 1)
#> 
#> [[3]][[2]]
#> (5)(2 3)
#> 
#> [[3]][[3]]
#> (5)(0 2)(1 3)
#> 
#> 
get_minimal_bsgs(c(2, 0), list(Permutation(c(1, 0, 2, 3, 5, 4)), Permutation(c(2, 3, 0, 1, 4, 5))))
#> [[1]]
#> [1] 0 2
#> 
#> [[2]]
#> [[2]][[1]]
#> (0 1)(4 5)
#> 
#> [[2]][[2]]
#> (5)(0 2)(1 3)
#> 
#> [[2]][[3]]
#> (2 3)(4 5)
#> 
#>
